scores.evidence: There are four can-do objectives with Bloom levels. Each one has an inline item and an exam item: o1 q1/q5, o2 q2/q6, o3 q3/q7, o4 q4 plus q8/q10/q9. Apply-level transfer items appear in the exam (q5 料理教室, q7 水やり記録).

hook-b1 sets up a concrete failure in 3 sentences (「グラフや分類が並んだ画面がすぐにできました。でも、ほしかったのは「月の途中で食費の使いすぎに気づける」ことでした。」). There is no trivia. The ungraded predict q0 leads into the goal-first idea that 2-1 and 2-2 resolve.

Prerequisites list ch0/ch1. s1-b1 recalls ch0's ビジョン, and ex-data recalls ch1's データベース. Terms are defined in definitions blocks before the quizzes use them. However, the q4 explanation names 「Claude Codeの公式ガイド（Anthropic）」, and neither ch0 nor ch1 mentions Claude Code (grep finds no match).

Each segment has one idea and at most 2 new terms (壁打ち / 目的・機能 / MVP・MoSCoW / 1枚企画書・PRD), and lint reports 0 length warnings. Section 2-3 (id 2-3) is dense: a two-paragraph lead, a definition, 6 steps each with expect, a diagram, a long model plan, then a quiz. PRD is introduced there and never used again.

s3-steps is a 6-step worked example with subgoal titles and a stated why for each step (e.g. ex-data 「決めないと、AIが推測で項目を選びます。」). It ends in the full model plan in s2-b3.expect. There is no faded example in this lesson; fading happens in the separate vibe-ch2-practice lesson.

All 4 content sections end in an inline check set in a new context, every wrong option has feedback, and q2 and q6 discriminate well. q3 is close to answerable by matching words: the goal 「読んだ本の感想を、あとで読み返せるように残す」 is paraphrased only by option b 「感想を書きとめて、あとから一覧で開ける機能」, so the Must test is barely exercised.

The body corrects the brief's misconceptions with reasons: s1-b5 (AI can't read your mind), s3-b1 (最初から完璧でなくてかまいません), s5-b1 (more features means more to check), and s2-table / s2-goal (feature vs goal). Every wrong option names a real belief in at most 2 sentences, e.g. q2 a 「「見られる」の形でも、中身は…機能です」 and q10 b 「消すと、次の版の候補も失われます」.

s2-b4 is a 3-node process diagram with a takeaway caption (「Mustだけなら、最初の版の画面は2つで足りる」), alt text and a description, and there are no decorative images. Node B reads 「食費の予算・使った額・残り」, while the alt and the Must in s5-b2 say the budget is set (「予算の設定」) on that screen. The figure does not show that step.

s1-b5 has the learner try s1-b4 with their own idea and compare the result with 「期待される結果」, which is the reader's actual expect label. s2-b3 gives a complete model plan. The hint ladder and checklist practice is in vibe-ch2-practice, which course.json lists as this lesson's next.

Four summary points come after the exam. summary-next has a reflection question (「Won'tに入れる機能は何でしょう？　理由も1つ考えてみましょう。」) and a next step. There are 6 flashcards that match the definitions, plus askTutor.

I re-fetched cc-best-practices. It does say "Claude can infer intent, but it can't read your mind", "…can produce code that solves the wrong problem" and "The most useful specs … state what is out of scope", which supports s1-b5 and the q4 explanation. The MVP and MoSCoW definitions match ries-mvp and abc-moscow, and s5-b3 / ex-moscow present the rules as lesson conventions (「このレッスンでは」). One small gap: s1-b5 extends a Claude-specific source to AI in general.

The text is warm です・ます throughout with no banned phrases. Terms are consistent (通知, 画面の流れ, 扱うデータ, and 「やらないこと」 quoted where it names the heading). The q4 explanation ending 「範囲外を書く、としています」 reads a little stiff.

Every learner-facing string has jp and en with matching meaning, including the diagram labels, alt and description in s2-b4. s1-b5 EN even quotes the reader's EN expect label ("What a good answer looks like"). validate reports 0 errors and lint --strict 0 warnings, and no text is baked into images.

niceToHave: active / s5-check q3: make the Must judgment real by replacing option d with a goal-related feature that is still not a Must. Option d md jp 「感想にタグを付けて、キーワードで探せる機能」 / en "Tagging your notes so you can search them by keyword"; feedback jp 「読み返しに役立ちますが、一覧から開ければ目的は果たせます。Mustではなく、Shouldの候補です。」 / en "It helps with rereading, but opening notes from the list already meets the goal. It's a Should candidate, not a Must." Key stays b.

miscon / s1-check q1 option b feedback: the current 「目的を一言そえても、提案を頼むとAIの答えが先に来ます。」 reads as if asking for feature suggestions is always wrong, but ex-ideas then does exactly that once the goal is set. Replace with jp 「目的が1文に決まる前に提案を頼むと、AIの答えが先に来ます。機能の候補は、目的が決まってから出してもらいます。」 / en "Asking for suggestions before the goal is a clear sentence puts the AI's answers first. Ask for candidate features once the goal is set."

prior / s3-check q4 explanation: Claude Code has not been introduced in ch0–ch2. Replace 「Claude Codeの公式ガイド（Anthropic）も、役に立つ仕様書（企画書のような文書）には範囲外を書く、としています。」 with 「AIの開発元Anthropicのガイドにも、役に立つ仕様書（企画書のような文書）には範囲外を書く、とあります。」 / en "A guide from Anthropic, an AI developer, likewise says useful specs (documents like this plan) state what is out of scope."

visual / s2-b4: make node B show where the budget is set, matching s5-b2 and the alt. jp node B 「今月の残り画面
予算の設定・使った額・残り」 / en "Money-left screen
set budget, spent, left".

miscon / check-quiz q7 option d feedback: it explains why posting is not needed but not that the reminder is missing. Replace with jp 「投稿は「枯らさない」目的に必要なく、通知がないと水やりを忘れます。投稿はWon'tにして、通知を入れます。」 / en "Posting isn't needed to keep plants alive, and without a reminder you'll still forget to water. Make posting a Won't and add the reminder."

worked / s5-b2, ex-moscow, s2-b3: the second Must 「今月の食費の予算の設定と残り金額の表示」 bundles two features, so the 「Mustは3つ以内」 rule of thumb looks like it is met by merging. Consider splitting it: ex-moscow.expect 「Mustは「食費の入力」「食費の予算の設定」「残り金額の表示」の3つになります。」, with the same three items in the s5-b2 Must cell and the s2-b3 model plan.
load / s3-defs: PRD is introduced but never used again. To save a term in the densest section, end the definition at 「…やらないことを、1枚に並べた文書です。」, or keep PRD only if a later chapter uses it.

align / o1: both o1 items (q1, q5) are option selection, while the objective says 「依頼文に書き換え」. The rewrite is practised only ungraded (s1-b5) and in vibe-ch2-practice. Acceptable, but an exam option set built from four rewrites of one vague request would test the rewriting more directly.
summary: Full review of the published vibe-ch2 (sha256:09186fc0e87a2e68). Its biggest strength is alignment: four objectives, each checked inline and in the exam with transfer contexts, plus well-built distractors (q2 a, q6, q10) whose feedback names real beliefs. The 6-step budget-app worked example states the why of every step. Every criterion is ≥ 3 (mean 3.38) and there is no must-fix item. The most useful improvement is to make q3 a real Must-vs-Should judgment and to align q1 b's feedback with ex-ideas, so learners don't conclude that asking an AI for feature ideas is always wrong.
